speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and have a known large ovarian mass. To help me narrow down the cause, does the abdominal swelling feel like fluid accumulation (ascites), and have you experienced any recent unintentional weight loss or loss of appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help characterize the ovarian mass, have you noticed any pelvic pain, bloating, or early satiety? Additionally, are you currently experiencing fever or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass and shortness of breath, I suspect pleural effusions, which would indicate Meigs' syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of prior malignancy, and have you noticed any urinary frequency or constipation due to the mass effect?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of a large ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with a normal CT scan otherwise, this strongly suggests Meigs' syndrome. I need to confirm the nature of the mass and rule out malignancy, so I will request an ultrasound and tumor markers. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound, REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present.; Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CA-125 level strongly supports a benign etiology, likely a fibroma, which fits the classic triad of Meigs' syndrome. I will now request medical images to visually confirm the solid nature of the ovarian mass and the extent of the ascites and pleural effusion. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the absence of systemic symptoms and bowel or urinary changes. With the triad of benign ovarian tumor, ascites, and pleural effusion now well-established, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs' syndrome
